status: Retrospective temporal holdout by fitting; all years were previously inspected in this repository
training_only_pooling: Starting at the highest fine bin, merge adjacent bins downward until each pooled class contains at least 20 complete training events for both declared resources; merge a remaining undersupported lowest class into its neighbor; retain original outer domain and actual pooled-bin widths
resource_definition: NOAA supplied XRS-B integrated irradiance over start-to-peak or start-to-end event windows, without additional background subtraction; band-limited fluence received at the instrument, not total flare energy
eligibility: Finite positive unsaturated peak irradiance within the closed fixed domain; resource-specific complete cases require finite positive fluence and a strictly positive corresponding event-window duration
cost_estimation: Separate arithmetic mean supplied fluence in each fixed bin; no power-law cost model and no fit to evaluation outcomes
conditioning: Predict shape conditional on the number of eligible 2024 events in the fixed domain; no prediction of absolute event rate or total fluence
uncertainty: Resample 12 calendar-month blocks with replacement within each year, independently for each training year and the evaluation year; share the same draws across forecasts and resource definitions
zero_bin_policy: Retain all bins; if a bootstrap training bin has no eligible events, mark that resource's replicate invalid rather than impute a mean cost or omit the bin; evaluation bins with zero events retain zero count/resource
intervals: Nominal 95% percentile month-block intervals; not simultaneous inference, a formal null calibration, completeness correction, or equivalence test
limitations: Retrospective reanalysis, not external preregistration or blinded validation
Instrument-derived peak and fluence share event definitions and measurements
No catalogue completeness, detection exposure or overlap correction
Missing end fluence can depend on peak irradiance
Temporal cost transfer may fail across solar-cycle phases
Month blocks do not cover all dependence or measurement uncertainty
Bin neutrality is a declared finite-class hypothesis; pooling uses training support only and binning is not changed after outcomes are scored
Broad pooled classes may have changing within-class size composition and therefore changing mean costs
